clue.text: In mansion, duke and I have become quieter

indicators.note: the duke is placed in the mansion, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a country seat is a grand house or mansion
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A duke and the narrator move into a stately home and grow calmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' is only a link. 'quieter' is not a comparative adjective here but a noun: something that quietens.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a drug that calms, so it is literally something that makes a person quiet.

clue.text: One reflective spectator losing almost everything as horse fails to finish

indicators.note: losing almost everything leaves just the first letter of the spectator word

parts.note: a seer is one who sees, a spectator

indicators.note: fails to finish means the last letter of the horse word is dropped

parts.note: equine means a horse or relating to horses

explanation.surface: A spectator loses nearly all their money when their horse fails to finish the race.
explanation.walkthrough: SEER is cut to S and EQUINE to EQUIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequin is a small shiny disc sewn onto clothes, and it catches and reflects light.

clue.text: Pulls grass up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the grass word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sward is an expanse of short grass

explanation.surface: Someone pulls up some grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw is to pull or drag, so draws means pulls.

clue.text: Almost hurl little boy in high chair

indicators.note: almost means the throwing word loses its final letter

parts.note: to throw is to hurl
Ned is a familiar short form of Edward, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A small boy nearly gets flung out of his highchair.
explanation.walkthrough: The high chair is not a baby's seat but a throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Throned means seated on a throne, the loftiest chair of state.

clue.text: Worthy failure to support new Bruges plant

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath

parts.note: a worthy is a notable person, a VIP

indicators.note: new means the letters of the town are made over in a new order

parts.note: a loss is a failure, as in a game

explanation.surface: A notable figure's flop props up some new venture in Bruges, Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' works because this is a down clue: the failure is written underneath. Bruges is a Belgian city, which makes the clue look like travel news.
explanation.definitionFit: Viper's bugloss is a blue-flowered wild plant of the borage family.

clue.text: Turning, bear left with a needless commotion

indicators.note: turning tells us to read the bear's name from right to left

parts.note: Pooh is the famous teddy bear of A. A. Milne's stories

explanation.surface: A bear spins round and leaves, causing a pointless fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is informal for a noisy fuss or ballyhoo, especially excitement over nothing much.

clue.text: Forecast: beware, elements changing

indicators.note: the two component words of the warning swap places

parts.note: the warning cry look out means beware

explanation.surface: A weather forecast warns people to beware as conditions change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elements' suggests the weather, but means the two parts of LOOK OUT trading places.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlook is a forecast of the future, such as a weather outlook.

clue.text: For Maid of the Mountains, holding fine correct text

parts.note: pro means for, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: holding means the nymph's name takes the fine letter inside

parts.note: an oread is a mountain nymph in Greek myth
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The text of the operetta The Maid of the Mountains needs correcting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Maid of the Mountains is a famous 1917 London musical, but here it is an oread, a mountain nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: To proofread is to read text and correct errors before publication.

clue.text: Following God? No expression of surprise, anyway

parts.note: after means following

indicators.note: no means without, so the surprise exclamation is removed

parts.note: Allah is the name of God in Islam
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A believer following God shows no surprise anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in any case or nonetheless, a synonym of anyway.

clue.text: Court, looking angry, imprisoning revolting beast

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a courtyard of a college

indicators.note: imprisoning has the angry word hold the revolting word inside it

parts.note: someone looking angry is red in the face
people who are in revolt are said to be up in arms, or simply up

explanation.surface: A courtyard with an angry face holds a disgusting animal captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like 'disgusting' but means rising up in rebellion: UP, as in 'the people are up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadruped is any four-footed animal, so a beast is a fair general example.

clue.text: He has urgent message: kill clause of bill

parts.note: to dispatch someone is to kill them
a rider is a clause added to a parliamentary bill

explanation.surface: A man carries a vital message about a clause in a bill that would allow killing.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcycle courier carries urgent messages, so the definition describes his job.

clue.text: Swimmer's brisk pace round bend

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: round says the brisk pace goes around the bend

parts.note: a trot is a brisk running pace
a U-bend or U-turn: U is a bend shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A swimmer moves at a brisk pace round a corner in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater fish, and fish are crosswords' favourite swimmers.

clue.text: Not so reasonable, hospital aboard ship not opening

indicators.note: aboard puts the hospital on board, inside the ship
not opening means the ship's word loses its first letter

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

explanation.surface: Unreasonably, a hospital has been set up on a ship that will not open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opening' asks for a ship word minus its first letter; 'aboard' then puts the hospital inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Insane means wildly unreasonable, so the comparative is less reasonable still.

clue.text: Sister swallows almost all hot drink, and she eats fast

indicators.note: swallows means the sister's abbreviation takes the drink inside it
almost all says drop the last letter of the drink

parts.note: coffee is a hot drink

explanation.surface: A nun gulps down most of a hot coffee, being a hasty eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'she eats fast' is the definition: fast means quickly, not going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is British slang for eating greedily and quickly, so one who does so is a scoffer.

clue.text: In Augusta, card blank -yell for correction

indicators.note: letters needing correction are wrong and must be rearranged

parts.note: used as written
used as written
used as written

explanation.surface: At the Augusta golf course, a player shouts to have a blank scorecard put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link. Augusta is a famous US golf course, which makes 'card' look like a scorecard. In fact it is the first name of Lady Bracknell, the formidable aunt in Oscar Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Bracknell's given name in Wilde's comedy is Augusta, so the forename identifies the character.

clue.text: Distinctive character I found in pieces of Telemann

indicators.note: found in places the letter I inside the rearranged composer
pieces of means the composer's name is broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A listener finds a distinctive quality in Telemann's compositions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces of' turns TELEMANN into LNEAMENT, with I added after the L. Telemann was a German Baroque composer, so 'pieces' look like musical works.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineament is a distinctive feature or characteristic, especially of the face.

clue.text: Ludicrous consequence of wrongly heating kiln?

definitions.meaning: a pot that has cracked from overheating in the kiln

explanation.surface: A potter's misjudged firing produces an absurd result.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective it means eccentric and absurd, and literally it is a broken pot.

clue.text: Frightened, feeling race tension?

definitions.meaning: acting out of fear, desperate to avoid a threat
read literally, nervous while taking part in a race

explanation.surface: A competitor is nervous before a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting in a panic, and taken literally it describes a fearful runner.

clue.text: Where Gary is at home, some help turned up

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the help phrase is read from the bottom

parts.note: some help is an aid

explanation.surface: A man named Gary is at home when some help arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes DIANA of AN AID. Gary is a city in this US state, birthplace of the Jackson family.
explanation.definitionFit: Gary is an industrial city on Lake Michigan in the US state of Indiana.

clue.text: Diamond in this form wins Sue's heart

indicators.note: heart means take only the middle, dropping the outer letters

parts.note: to sue is to prosecute, taking someone to court

explanation.surface: A diamond cut in a particular style wins a woman's love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wins' is a link. 'Sue' is not a woman but the verb, prosecute; removing its outer P and E gives the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose cut is a way of shaping a diamond with a flat base and triangular facets rising to a point.

clue.text: Very small period of life, a year

parts.note: the teens are the years from thirteen to nineteen
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A small child's age is given in years.
explanation.definitionFit: Teensy is an informal word for tiny, very small.

clue.text: Hero-worshipper's praise I accepted in company

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: accepted in means taken inside the company's abbreviation

parts.note: to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: A fan of heroes receives praise from the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero is not a champion but the heroine of Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing, whom Claudio loves and plans to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: In Much Ado About Nothing, Claudio is the young lord who falls for Hero, so he literally worships her.

clue.text: Farcical, to be provoked over one empty barrel

indicators.note: over means the provoked word spreads across, covering the rest

parts.note: to rise is to react when provoked, as a fish rises to bait
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: empty means take out the inside, keeping just the outer letters

explanation.surface: A ridiculous scene: someone is provoked into a fury over an empty barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means covering or round, not above, so the provoked word encloses the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means laughable, ridiculous enough to be comic, which is what farcical means.

clue.text: Fish from river held in beak

indicators.note: held in means the river letter is placed inside the beak

parts.note: a bird's bill is its beak

explanation.surface: A bird holds a fish from the river in its beak.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is a European flatfish related to the turbot.

clue.text: Greek PE is a work of art

parts.note: the Greek letter written like a P in its capital form here is taken as pi
the Greek letter for E is taken as eta, whose capital looks like H but sounds E

explanation.surface: A school PE lesson in Greece is a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PE' looks like school gym class but is two letters, each spelt out as a Greek letter name. Strictly a Greek capital P is rho, and an initial E would be epsilon, so the setter is matching sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, so a specific kind of artwork.

clue.text: At first, secondary schooling not a temptation

indicators.note: at first means use only the opening letter of the next word
not a says remove one letter A from the schooling word

parts.note: schooling is education

explanation.surface: Early in secondary school, a pupil turns away from temptation.
explanation.definitionFit: Seduction is the act of enticing someone, so it is close to a temptation.

clue.text: Result of sitting in sun: absorbing it, I become red

indicators.note: absorbing means the result of sunbathing soaks up the rest inside it

parts.note: a tan is what sunbathing produces

explanation.surface: After sunbathing, the narrator turns red as a lobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' is a link. Titian is a reddish-gold colour, named for the hair in the Venetian painter's portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian is a shade of reddish-brown or auburn named after the Venetian painter, so a kind of red.

clue.text: Rally, but beaten without mercy

indicators.note: beaten, as eggs are beaten, leaves the letters mixed up

parts.note: used as written
used as written

explanation.surface: A team rallies but still loses heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something brutally means doing it savagely, which is acting without mercy.
